correctness.rationale: In the strictly positive regime, the normalized seed allocation equation gives the unique attracting positive occupancy p*=(ch-e[h+phi(1-h)])/(c+e(gamma-1)), with c>e forced by viability. Its disturbance derivative is -c[phi(1-h)+gamma h]/[c+e(gamma-1)]^2<0. The exact linear balance U=(h-p)/e=phi/c(1-h)+(h-p)/c+gamma/c*p proves rank equivalence to noncollinearity of observed (h,p). Rank deficiency gives an open biological parameter fiber, not just a formal algebraic ambiguity. The L-design determinant (h2-h1)(p3-p1) never vanishes under the stated positive-occupancy and distinct-control assumptions, and explicit inversion recovers every unknown. A complete rational counterparameter curve and 2500 grid checks were executed with standalone standard-library code; the infinite theorem rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: The original normalized directed-dispersal model and its equilibrium response are fully credited to Purves and Dushoff 2005. The reviewed accessible model and fitting sections discuss curves and nonunique baseline fitting but not the necessary-and-sufficient noncollinearity criterion for jointly recovering all three unknown biological parameters, the universally nonsingular feasible three-setting design, or the single-axis impossibility. The closest other accessible scientific materials treat a general framework or detection-error identification and do not imply this particular model-specific global inversion. Published research-record comparisons concerned different ecological mechanisms. Search failure is not a proof of priority; the original supplementary appendix and a broader 2002 technical paper remain material historical risks.
residual_risks: The 2005 source-model supplemental appendix was inaccessible at its published link; its contents were not asserted non-covering.
Full technical text of the more general 2002 metapopulation framework was not materially inspected; exact stronger coverage cannot be ruled out.
More extensive historical searching might uncover a prior model-specific experimental-design theorem; no claim of independently certified novelty.
The model-specific proof uses elementary linear algebra; the contribution is the sharp ecological identifiability boundary and universally feasible mixed-control design, not new linear algebra.

value.rationale: The originally motivated ecological model has three distinct unknown biological quantities but typical habitat- or disturbance-only calibration produces confounding. The claim exactly characterizes when mechanistic inference is possible and provides a minimal three-environment design guaranteed nonsingular whenever all regimes maintain positive equilibrium. The otherwise counterintuitive failure of arbitrarily many one-control surveys is biologically meaningful for selecting habitat/disturbance perturbations. Determinant magnitude explicitly exposes structural conditioning. The theorem is limited to exact deterministic equilibria and does not claim empirical noisy estimation or a new general linear-algebra lemma.
